title: The Back Acupoint Localization Method Based on Bone-Measuring Method and HRFormer-MMFA Fusion Network
content: Chinese Medicine (CM), a therapeutic system refined over thousands of years of practice, has demonstrated significant efficacy in the prevention and treatment of numerous diseases. Among its many practices, acupoint therapy holds a crucial position in Chinese Medicine clinical practice. Acupuncture and other techniques can effectively alleviate pain and treat diseases, with precise acupoint localization being the primary prerequisite for such treatments.In this study, we propose an intelligent acupoint recognition method for the back based on the "Bone-Measuring Method." By integrating the HRFormer feature extraction network, Multi-Matrix Fusion Attention (MMFA), and a multi-level joint loss function, combined with a pixel-physiological size dynamic conversion algorithm, we achieve anatomically standardized acupoint localization.Specifically, we first embed the MMFA module into a parallel multi-resolution structure to more efficiently capture multi-scale features and use a multi-level joint loss function for end-to-end optimization. Second, based on the anatomical principles of the traditional "Bone-Measuring Method," we design a pixel-physiological size dynamic conversion algorithm to map image coordinates to a standardized physiological size space, addressing localization deviations caused by individual body size differences. Finally, by enhancing the feature representation capability of the Transformer block through detail-specific feed forward layers, we achieve feature aggregation using intra- and inter-feature interaction transformers.Experimental results on our self-built dataset show that our proposed HRFormer + MMFA + multi-level joint loss method performs exceptionally well in Chinese Medicine acupoint recognition tasks, significantly outperforming existing mainstream models. It achieves a Normalized Mean Error (NME) of 0.6% and a Failure Rate at 1 cm (FR@1cm) of 1.2% on the standard test set, while maintaining real-time inference (18 FPS) with a precision of 96.8% and an AUC value of 0.97. Moreover, the model maintains stable performance in complex scenarios, such as obese body types and occlusions, demonstrating good generalization ability and clinical applicability. In summary, our proposed model can automatically and accurately assess back acupoints, potentially providing strong support for Chinese Medicine practitioners' treatment decisions and effectively assisting Chinese Medicine clinical therapy.
